messages.content: I’m ready to reserve Denver. The official block room opened back up, but it’s the one-queen room with no breakfast and the earlier cancellation date. Can you help me make the final call on flights and hotel before I click through?

Yes. I’d keep the flight plan we discussed: Sunday afternoon nonstop SLC to Denver so you can check in without rushing, and the Wednesday midafternoon nonstop after the closing lunch. On the hotel, the trade-off is clear: the official block wins for being in or next to the meeting flow, while the nearby breakfast-included hotel wins on easy mornings. Since your Monday roundtable is now the anchor, I’d book the official block and solve breakfast separately.
That’s where I’m leaning. I would rather be close to the meeting rooms. No rental car, one queen is fine for just me, and please request window seats on the flights if they’re selectable.

Good. For the flights, choose a fare that lets you select seats and avoid basic economy if the price difference is modest. Request window seats on both legs; if the only windows left are paid preferred seats, you can either pay only if it is reimbursable or set a reminder to check again at online check-in. For the hotel, the one-queen official block room is appropriate for a solo trip. Confirm the rate is about $219 before taxes, no required parking charge because you will not have a car, and no destination or facility fee.
Should I also hold the Hampton backup for the breakfast, or is that just creating another thing to cancel?

If the block room checks out as refundable until June 14 at 5 p.m., I would skip the Hampton backup. Hampton is easier for breakfast, but being farther from the sessions is the wrong inconvenience for this agenda. I’d only hold Hampton for a day if the official block page shows a surprise fee, a nonrefundable rule, or a rate above the reimbursement cap.
Okay. Ground transport from DEN: still train first?

Yes, train first if it is running normally when you land. Take the A Line to Union Station, then either walk if the hotel is truly close and the weather is fine, or use a short rideshare for the last hop. Keep the train receipt and any rideshare receipt. If your flight is delayed, you have a heavier bag than expected, or there is service disruption, go straight to rideshare from the airport and document it.
The hotel page confirms cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. local time, parking is $49 but optional, and I don’t see a destination fee.

That is bookable. Take screenshots of the cancellation rule, nightly rate, taxes, and the no-fee/optional-parking language. Add a calendar reminder for June 14 at noon so you have time to cancel before the 5 p.m. deadline if anything changes.
Breakfast is the only thing I’m still uneasy about. I don’t want Monday to start with a scramble.

Plan it simply: Sunday dinner downtown after check-in; Monday buy breakfast near the hotel before 9:45, then head to the roundtable area early. Check whether the conference provides coffee or pastries Tuesday and Wednesday, but do not rely on it. For dinners, use the conference reception if one is included; otherwise pick something within a short walk of the hotel so you are not managing transportation at night.
Flights and block room are booked. Give me the final booking note for my file.

Denver conference booking note: booked Sunday June 23 nonstop SLC-DEN in the afternoon, arriving with time for downtown check-in; booked Wednesday June 26 nonstop DEN-SLC around 4:45 p.m. after the closing lunch. Window seats requested/selected where available; verify seat numbers again at check-in. Hotel: official downtown conference block, one-queen room, about $219 before taxes, cancel by June 14 at 5 p.m. local time. No rental car. Use A Line to Union Station plus walk/short rideshare; rideshare direct from DEN only if delayed or train service is disrupted. Meals: no included hotel breakfast, so budget quick paid breakfasts and use nearby downtown dinners. Reimbursement file: airfare receipt, hotel confirmation, cancellation screenshot, hotel folio, train/rideshare receipts, and meal receipts if allowed.

messages.content: Denver is in four days. The app added Sunday evening badge pickup, and Monday seating starts earlier than the old agenda. Also, I saw a note about A Line evening maintenance. Can we tighten the timing?

Yes. Assuming the Sunday flight still lands around 3:18, you have enough cushion, but I would not make the train the only plan. Use the A Line if service looks normal when you land; otherwise take rideshare straight from DEN. The goal is hotel by about 5, badge pickup shortly after, then dinner.
Correct, 3:18 landing, carry-on only. Badge pickup is 5 to 7 Sunday.

Sunday plan: land 3:18, check the RTD alert before leaving the gate, and if the A Line is running normally, aim for the next train and a short transfer from Union Station. If there is a maintenance delay longer than 15 to 20 minutes, switch to rideshare. Either way, check in first if the hotel is on the way, then go to badge pickup around 5:30 or 5:45.
Monday seating starts at 10:30 now, with the roundtable at 11. No hotel breakfast.

Monday: be dressed and out for breakfast by 8:45. Pick a quick paid option within a block or two, or grab coffee/yogurt from the hotel market if the line is long. Return to the room by 9:45, take materials with you by 10:10, and be in the seating area at 10:25. If you miss Sunday badge pickup, shift earlier and go to registration around 9:45.
Wednesday closing lunch ends at 1. Flight is about 4:45. What should I do with bags?

Wednesday checklist: check out before sessions and leave your bag with the bell desk; keep laptop, ID, and any receipts with you. After the closing lunch, leave by 1:10, pick up the bag, and depart the hotel by 1:25. Rideshare is the safest buffer for a 4:45 flight; train is okay only if service is clean and you are moving by about 1:20. Target DEN by 2:15, which leaves room for security, a snack, and any gate change.

messages.content: Denver is done, so I’m starting the late-August Pacific Northwest loop. Draft is: Monday high-school visits in Portland, Tuesday evening college fair in Beaverton, Wednesday 8 a.m. counselor breakfast in Eugene, Thursday afternoon Tacoma visit, and Thursday evening Seattle fair. Can you compare open-jaw versus round-trip Portland, car versus rail, and hotel bases with breakfast and easy dinner access?

Yes. One detail will affect the Thursday plan: where is the Seattle fair, downtown or somewhere like Bellevue/Northgate? With the schedule as written, I already lean open-jaw into Portland and home from Seattle, with a rental car, but the Seattle venue decides whether Thursday night should be downtown, SeaTac, or Southcenter.

Seattle fair is at the downtown convention center, 6 to 8 p.m. Tacoma visit is 1:30 Thursday. Beaverton fair is 6:30 to 8:30 Tuesday. Monday visits are Portland proper and one NE Portland school. I’ll have a rolling bag plus one small materials box.

Here’s the practical routing comparison. Open-jaw SLC-PDX and SEA-SLC with a one-way rental car: best schedule, no backtracking after the Seattle fair, and easiest for materials; likely higher than a Portland round trip because of the one-way car fee. Round-trip Portland: cheaper airfare, but after Seattle you either drive three hours late Thursday or wake up very early Friday to get back to PDX. Rail hybrid: workable on paper, but fragile with materials and multiple suburban stops. Recommendation: open-jaw plus rental car.
The Portland round trip may be about $150 cheaper in airfare. Is the backtracking still that bad?

For this itinerary, yes. The Thursday Seattle fair ends at 8, so a same-night drive to Portland means a late arrival near midnight before flying the next day. Waiting until Friday means a predawn drive with traffic and no cushion. That savings is not worth the fatigue and missed-flight risk unless the open-jaw price is dramatically worse after the rental quote.
Open-jaw then. Look at nonstop holds. If Delta lines up, that’s fine, but I don’t want to force a bad time or a connection.

Nonstop shortlist: Sunday SLC-PDX, Delta around 2:10 to 3:15 or Alaska around 4:25 to 5:30. Friday SEA-SLC, Delta around 1:15 to 4:05 or Alaska around 3:05 to 5:55. I’d hold the Delta 2:10 outbound and 1:15 return if pricing is close because the times fit cleanly. Avoid connections for this loop. Request window seats after ticketing if they are available.
The 2:10 Sunday departure works, and Friday 1:15 is fine if I’m staying near SeaTac Thursday. What about car versus train?

Rent the car. Rail would add transfers, rideshares, and schedule risk between Portland, Beaverton, Eugene, Tacoma, and downtown Seattle. Car hold: pick up at PDX Sunday around 3:45 or 4, return at SEA Friday around 11:30, midsize car or compact SUV, one-way drop allowed. Verify the one-way fee, total taxes, and whether parking is reimbursable.
Hotels are the bigger thing. I want easy breakfast, and Tuesday night needs dinner solved because I’ll get to Eugene late.

Best base pattern: Sunday and Monday in Beaverton/Tigard for Portland and the Tuesday fair; Tuesday night in Eugene; Wednesday night in Federal Way or Tacoma; Thursday night SeaTac/Southcenter. Hotel ideas: Hyatt House Beaverton or Hampton Beaverton area for breakfast and nearby restaurants; Home2 Suites Eugene Downtown/University or Hyatt Place Oakway for breakfast or close food; Hampton/Fairfield in Federal Way for breakfast and free parking; Homewood or Hampton near Southcenter/SeaTac for breakfast, dinner access, and an easy Friday airport run.
Would Salem be smarter Tuesday night so I’m not driving all the way to Eugene after the Beaverton fair?

Salem is easier Tuesday night but worse Wednesday morning. Beaverton to Salem after the fair is about 55 to 75 minutes; Salem to Eugene in the morning is another 65 to 80, and you’d need to leave around 6:15 for an 8 a.m. breakfast. Driving to Eugene Tuesday is closer to two hours and a late arrival, but it protects the breakfast. I’d choose Eugene and plan dinner before the fair or bring something for the drive.
Let’s do Eugene. Cancellable queen rooms, no prepaid if possible. Parking needs to be clear for reimbursement.

Good. Holds I’d place: Beaverton/Tigard for Sunday-Monday, queen room, breakfast included, parking fee shown clearly; Eugene Tuesday, queen room, late-arrival note, breakfast start verified; Federal Way Wednesday, queen room, breakfast and free or clearly priced parking; Southcenter/SeaTac Thursday, queen room, breakfast, and restaurants nearby. For each one, screenshot cancellation deadline, nightly rate, parking language, and breakfast details.
For Wednesday, Federal Way might make Thursday easier than Tacoma, right?

Yes. Federal Way splits the difference well. It is usually 20 to 30 minutes to Tacoma, but allow 45. After the 1:30 Tacoma visit, leave for downtown Seattle by about 3:15 or 3:30, park once, eat early near the convention center, and walk into the fair without trying to check into a downtown hotel.
Can I avoid downtown Seattle hotel parking Thursday?

Yes. Use downtown parking only for the fair, then drive to Southcenter or SeaTac afterward. That avoids an overnight downtown hotel parking charge and puts you close to the airport for Friday. If you are hungry after the fair, Southcenter has more late practical options than a random airport hotel block.
Give me the holds to place and what can wait. I’ll send this to my director with the rationale for the open-jaw cost.

Recommended holds: 1) Flights: hold Sunday SLC-PDX nonstop around 2:10 p.m. and Friday SEA-SLC nonstop around 1:15 p.m.; avoid connections. 2) Car: one-way rental, PDX pickup Sunday about 4 p.m., SEA return Friday about 11:30 a.m.; verify one-way fee and total taxes. 3) Hotels: Beaverton/Tigard Sunday-Monday with breakfast and dinner nearby; Eugene Tuesday with late-arrival note and breakfast verified; Federal Way Wednesday with breakfast/free or clearly priced parking; Southcenter or SeaTac Thursday with breakfast and easy Friday airport access. Rationale for director: open-jaw costs more than a Portland round trip, but it avoids a late-night or predawn three-hour backtrack after the Seattle fair, protects the Friday return, and reduces fatigue during a multi-city recruitment week. Can wait: final hotel choice within each area until school addresses are firm, exact car class unless materials increase, and seat selection until ticketing opens.
